turns.t: Doctor, I am not able to put the drops properly. Half goes on my cheek, half goes on my saree, and I am sure nothing goes in the eye.
Ah, very common problem, and nothing to be embarrassed about. Sit comfortably and tell me what happens when you try.
I tilt my head back, I hold the bottle high, and then at the last second I close my eyes. My grandson laughs at me, he says I am blinking before the drop even leaves the bottle.
So you are flinching. Everyone does it. The eye is very protective, like a goalkeeper, it shuts the gate when anything comes close.
Exactly like that. And my right eye has also started watering a lot, ever since I started struggling with this.
How long has the watering been going on?
Ten days, I think. Yes, ten days, because it began just before my sister's housewarming and she said, why are you crying at my party.
Ha. Is it only watering, or does it also hurt? Any pain in the eye?
No pain, no. Only watering, that is all, but it is very irritating.
And has the sight changed at all, any change in your vision, blurring or anything?
No, vision is the same as always. I can still thread a needle, that is my test.
Good test. Is that for work?
Yes, I stitch blouses at home for the ladies in our colony. Forty blouses before Diwali, last year, I did. So my eyes are very important to me.
I can see that. And you have glaucoma, if I read your file correctly. How long has it been?
Two years now. The earlier doctor told me, pressure in the eye can damage the nerve silently, so I must be regular.
He told you right. That is why getting the drops into the eye matters so much. Let's fix your technique today, instead of me just telling you to try harder.
Please. My neighbour says she puts them lying on the sofa, and her husband holds the bottle.
That works for some people, but you don't need a husband. Think of your lower eyelid as a little pocket. Put your finger just under the eye and gently pull the skin down, so the pocket opens.
Like this? My finger is shaking a little.
Perfect. Now look up at the ceiling, and bring the bottle close, not so high. Imagine you are watering a tiny plant, you don't pour it from the roof.
I am looking at the ceiling. There is a spot on the ceiling, by the way. It looks like a map of Sri Lanka.
I'll mention it to the maintenance team. Now squeeze one drop only, into the pocket, and keep looking up while it lands.
One drop. Oh! It went in. I felt it go in. It was cold.
That's it. Now close your eyes gently, don't squeeze them shut, and press lightly with one finger in the inner corner near your nose for a minute.
Why the nose corner? Is that a secret?
Not a secret. It is like putting your thumb over a tap, it stops the drop draining away down the little channel into the nose, so it stays in the eye longer and does its work.
Oh, I never knew. My drops were running down my own nose all this time.
Quite likely. Wait five minutes between two different drops, if you ever use more than one, and wash your hands before you start.
Wash hands, pocket, one drop, press the corner. I will write it on a card and stick it on the bathroom mirror.
Excellent idea. Practise a few times in front of the mirror with your grandson watching, and let him be the judge.
He will love that, he has been a judge of my cricket also. The watering, will it stop?
I'm sure better technique will help a lot with the cheek, and if you blink less, you'll waste less. Let's see how it goes.
Okay, doctor. Should I come back to show you?
Yes, I'd like to see you in three weeks. Bring the bottle, and I'll watch you put one in on your own.
Three weeks. I will practise every morning, like a homework.
Do that. And no stitching blouses until the drop is in, or you will be telling the blouse about your eye.
Ha, ha. Thank you, doctor. I will not close my eyes this time, I promise.

chief_complaint.value: I am not able to put the drops properly

symptoms.name: my right eye has also started watering

clinical_actions.description: Eye-drop technique: pull lower lid into a pocket, look up, one drop, close eyes gently and press inner corner for a minute, wash hands
